info.title: Pilot API
info.description:
User/Pilot API endpoints requiring OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE. These endpoints access user-specific data and require the pilot's explicit consent.

## Quick Start

The Pilot API uses the **Authorization Code + PKCE** flow (no client secret needed). See the **OAuth** section below for full endpoint documentation with parameters and examples.

### Flow Overview

1. Generate a random `code_verifier` (43-128 chars) and compute `code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier))`
2. Redirect the pilot to `GET /oauth/authorize` with your client_id, scopes, and the code_challenge
3. Pilot logs in and consents — vAMSYS redirects back to your `redirect_uri` with a `code`
4. Exchange the `code` + `code_verifier` at `POST /oauth/token` to receive an access token and refresh token
5. Call Pilot API endpoints with `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`
6. When the token expires (1 hour), use the refresh token at `POST /oauth/token` to get a new one

### Example: Making an API Request

```
GET /api/v3/pilot/profile
Authorization: Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1Q...
Accept: application/json
```

## Token Information
- **Access token expiry**: 1 hour (3600 seconds). First-party vAMSYS clients receive a longer expiry.
- **Refresh tokens**: Included — use to obtain new access tokens without re-prompting the pilot
- **PKCE**: Mandatory — this is a public client, no client secret is used

## Security Considerations
- **Store tokens securely** — treat access and refresh tokens as sensitive credentials
- **Use HTTPS only** — OAuth flows must occur over secure connections
- **Validate state parameter** — always verify the `state` returned matches what you sent to prevent CSRF
- **Refresh proactively** — refresh tokens before they expire to avoid interrupting the user

## Handling Revoked Tokens & Withdrawn Consent

A pilot can revoke your application's access at any time, and the VA owner can deactivate your client. When this happens:

- **API requests** will return `401 Unauthenticated`
- **Refresh token requests** will return `400` with `error: "invalid_grant"`

Your application should handle both cases gracefully:

1. On `401` — try refreshing the token first
2. If refresh also fails (`400 invalid_grant`) — the consent has been revoked
3. Discard stored tokens and prompt the pilot to re-authorize via `GET /oauth/authorize`

## Rate Limiting
- 100 requests per minute per airline
- All OAuth clients for an airline share the same rate limit pool
- Monitor `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Limit` headers

get.description:
Returns the pilot's most recent logbook entry for the activity.
Returns 404 if the pilot has no progress recorded yet.

post.description:
Registers the pilot for an activity. For Tour, Roster and CuratedRoster
activities a progress logbook is created alongside the registration.
Returns 422 if the registration window is not open, the pilot is already
registered, or the activity does not allow repeat participation and has
already been completed by the pilot.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a registration belonging to the pilot, along with any
in-progress (Incomplete) logbook for the activity. Returns 404 if the
registration does not exist or belongs to a different pilot.

get.description:
Returns a cursor-paginated list of flight bookings for the authenticated pilot.
Use the status filter to switch between current (active), past (deleted without PIREP),
completed (deleted with PIREP), and all bookings.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Available sorts are `id`, `created_at`, `departure_time`. You can sort by multiple options by separating them with a comma. To sort in descending order, use `-` sign in front of the sort, for example: `-id`.

parameters.name: page[size]
parameters.description: The number of results that will be returned per page.

parameters.name: page[cursor]
parameters.description: The cursor to start the pagination from.

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

post.description:
Creates a new flight booking for the authenticated pilot.
The route must belong to the pilot's airline, be bookable, and not hidden.
The aircraft must be compatible with the route's fleet types and not hidden.

503.description: A booking is already being created for this pilot; retry shortly

get.description:
Returns a specific booking belonging to the authenticated pilot.
Includes soft-deleted bookings so pilots can inspect cancelled or completed bookings.

delete.description:
Cancels the specified booking and all subsequent bookings for the authenticated pilot.
Any associated PIREPs will also be deleted.
Cannot cancel if the booking has position reports created within the last 5 minutes.

message.const: Booking has recent position reports. Wait 5 minutes after stopping tracking.

get.description:
Returns the most recently linked SimBrief OFP for the specified booking.
Returns 404 if no OFP has been linked yet.

put.description:
Links an externally-generated SimBrief OFP to the booking using the pilot's
Navigraph account. The OFP's departure and arrival airports must match the
booked route — returns 422 `route_mismatch` if they differ or the OFP does
not contain airport identifiers.

The `dispatch_id` must be an identifier SimBrief's v2 flight plan API accepts:
the numeric `request_id` from the OFP parameters, or the OFP's `static_id`.
The `ofp_id` value appended to SimBrief's v1 dispatch redirect URL is not a
valid lookup key and returns 422 `invalid_dispatch_id`.

Requires the pilot to have a Navigraph account linked in vAMSYS.

post.description:
Creates a dispatch session and returns a Phoenix URL for the pilot to complete
the full dispatch form (SimBrief, cargo, containers, etc.). Phoenix creates
the booking when the pilot submits the form.

422.description: Route invalid, hidden, or not bookable

get.description:
Returns a cursor-paginated list of all manual PIREP claims for the authenticated pilot.
Filter: `filter[status]=pending|waiting|accepted|rejected`

parameters.name: page[size]

parameters.name: page[cursor]
parameters.description: The cursor to start the pagination from.

post.description:
Submits a manual PIREP claim for the specified booking. Creates a pending claim
with proof attachments, creates an associated PIREP of type 'claim', updates
the pilot's location to the arrival airport, and deletes the booking.

Proof items: each must be `{"type": "image", "data": "data:image/...;base64,..."}` or
`{"type": "link", "url": "https://..."}`. Between 1 and 5 items required.
Images are stored on DigitalOcean Spaces (max 10MB each, JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP).

get.description: Returns full detail for a single claim including proof attachments and review status.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the claim and its associated PIREP. Only `pending` claims
can be deleted. Returns 422 if the claim is not in pending status.

get.description: Returns all aircraft the pilot has marked as favourite at this airline.
Returns all airports the pilot has marked as favourite at this airline.

post.description:
Adds or removes an aircraft from the pilot's favourites.
Returns 201 with the aircraft data when added, 204 when removed.
Returns 422 if the aircraft does not belong to the pilot's airline.

Adds or removes an airport from the pilot's favourites by ICAO code.
Returns 201 with the airport data when added, 204 when removed.
Returns 422 if the airport is not found in the pilot's airline.

get.description:
Returns all NOTAMs for the pilot's airline, with `is_read` indicating
whether the authenticated pilot has acknowledged each NOTAM.

Filter: `filter[active]=true` restricts to currently visible NOTAMs.
Filter: `filter[must_read]=true` restricts to must-read NOTAMs only.

post.description:
Records that the authenticated pilot has read/acknowledged this NOTAM.
Idempotent — calling multiple times has no additional effect.
Returns 404 if the NOTAM does not belong to the pilot's airline.

delete.description:
Removes the authenticated pilot's read acknowledgment for this NOTAM.
Idempotent — returns 204 even if the acknowledgment did not exist.
Returns 404 if the NOTAM does not belong to the pilot's airline.

Returns a cursor-paginated list of PIREPs for the authenticated pilot.
Use the status filter to narrow results by flight status.

get.description:
Returns a specific PIREP belonging to the authenticated pilot.
Includes soft-deleted PIREPs.
Returns all comments for the specified PIREP belonging to the authenticated pilot.

post.description:
Adds a comment to the specified PIREP belonging to the authenticated pilot.
Cannot comment on PIREPs that are still being processed.
Posting a comment moves the PIREP back to failed status and clears the reply-needed flag,
mirroring the behaviour of the Phoenix UI.

422.description: Cannot comment on a processing PIREP

get.description:
Returns all position reports for a specific PIREP belonging to the authenticated pilot.
Results are ordered oldest-first (ascending by id) for flight replay and track rendering.

Returns altitude, groundspeed, and event annotations in chart-ready format.
Each data point is {x: timestamp_ms, y: value}. Returns empty arrays
if no position reports are available.

post.description:
Creates an immediately-accepted PIREP from an existing booking.
The booking is deleted after the PIREP is created (same as normal flight flow).
Activity bonuses (tours, events, rosters, community goals) are calculated
asynchronously and added to the PIREP's bonus_sum.

These PIREPs appear in the pilot's logbook but do not have an internal
detail page — use redirect_url to link pilots to your own platform for
full flight data.
post.summary: Create a VA PIREP from a booking

get.description:
Returns the current pilot's full profile for this airline. The pilot is
resolved from the OAuth token's airline — no other airline data is accessible.

Returns comprehensive flight statistics broken down by time period
(today, yesterday, last 24h, last 30 days, year-to-date, last year, all-time).
All statistics are scoped to this airline only.

Returns flight statistics grouped by aircraft type, online network,
route type, and day/night. Only accepted and complete PIREPs are counted.

Returns all badges earned by the pilot at this airline, ordered by
the date they were earned (most recent first).

Returns the pilot's current display rank (respects prefer_honorary_rank flag)
along with requirements and progress toward the next rank.
Returns 404 if no rank is assigned.

Returns all holidays for the pilot at this airline, ordered by start date
(most recent first). Returns an empty list if the airline does not have the
holiday feature enabled (check `holiday_allowance` on the pilot profile — it will be null).

post.description:
Creates a new holiday for the pilot. Returns 422 if the airline does not
have the holiday feature enabled (holiday_allowance is null on pilot profile).

patch.description:
Updates one or more pilot preferences. All fields are optional — only
the fields provided will be updated.

Sets or clears the pilot's current location airport.
Pass `airport_id: null` to clear the location.

422.description: Airport does not belong to the pilot airline

patch.description:
Sets or clears the pilot's current hub.
Pass `hub_id: null` to clear the hub.

422.description: Hub does not belong to the pilot airline

delete.description:
Deletes a holiday belonging to the pilot. Returns 404 if the holiday does
not exist or does not belong to the authenticated pilot.

get.description:
Returns a cursor-paginated list of the pilot's personal rosters,
ordered newest first.

Creates a new personal roster for the pilot from an ordered list of flights.

Returns 404 if the roster does not exist or belongs to a different pilot.

delete.description:

Returns 404 if the roster does not exist or belongs to a different pilot.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's profile and identity data. The response
is scoped by the OAuth token's granted scopes — only fields permitted by
the token's scopes are included.

Redirect the user's browser to this URL to begin the OAuth flow. The pilot will see a consent screen listing the requested scopes. After approving, they are redirected to your `redirect_uri` with `?code={authorization_code}&state={state}`.

### Preparing the Request

**1. Generate a code verifier** — a cryptographically random string of 43–128 characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `-`, `.`, `_`, `~`).

**2. Compute the code challenge:**
```
code_challenge = BASE64URL_ENCODE(SHA256(code_verifier))
```

**3. Build the authorization URL** with the query parameters documented below and redirect the pilot to it.

### Example URL
```
https://vamsys.io/oauth/authorize?
  client_id=42
  &redirect_uri=https://myapp.example.com/callback
  &response_type=code
  &scope=identity:basic pilot:read flights:read
  &state=random-csrf-string
  &code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM
  &code_challenge_method=S256
```
get.summary: Authorize — redirect the pilot here to start the PKCE flow

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Must exactly match the redirect URI registered for your client

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-separated list of scopes. Must include identity:basic at minimum.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Random string to prevent CSRF — verify it matches when the user returns

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) — the PKCE challenge derived from your secret code verifier

302.description:
Redirects the pilot to the vAMSYS consent screen. After the pilot approves, they are redirected to your `redirect_uri` with query parameters:

- `code` — the authorization code (use within 60 seconds)
- `state` — the same state value you sent (verify this matches!)

Example callback: `https://myapp.example.com/callback?code=def502003a7e...&state=xYz123-csrf-token`

post.description:
Exchange an authorization code (from the authorize redirect) or a refresh token for a new access token.

### Grant Type: authorization_code

After the pilot is redirected back to your app with a `code`, exchange it here.

**Required fields:** `grant_type`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `code`, `code_verifier`

```
POST /oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=authorization_code
&client_id=42
&redirect_uri=https://myapp.example.com/callback
&code=def502003a7e...
&code_verifier=dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk
```

### Grant Type: refresh_token

Use the `refresh_token` from a previous token response to get a new access token without prompting the pilot again.

**Required fields:** `grant_type`, `client_id`, `refresh_token`

```
POST /oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=refresh_token
&client_id=42
&refresh_token=def50200a4f5c8b3...
```
post.summary: Token — exchange authorization code or refresh token for an access token

grant_type.description: Use "authorization_code" for initial token exchange, or "refresh_token" to refresh an expired access token

redirect_uri.description: Required when grant_type=authorization_code. Must match the URI used in the authorize request.

code.description: Required when grant_type=authorization_code. The authorization code received at your redirect_uri.

code_verifier.description: Required when grant_type=authorization_code. The original PKCE code verifier string (before hashing).

refresh_token.description: Required when grant_type=refresh_token. The refresh token from a previous token response.

scope.description: Optional when grant_type=refresh_token. Must be a subset of the originally granted scopes.

expires_in.description: Token lifetime in seconds (3600 = 1 hour). Longer for first-party vAMSYS clients.

refresh_token.description: Use to obtain a new access token when the current one expires

400.description:
Invalid request. Common causes:

- `invalid_grant` — authorization code expired, code_verifier mismatch, refresh token revoked, or pilot withdrew consent
- `invalid_client` — client_id is invalid or the client has been deactivated by the VA owner

If you receive `invalid_grant` during a refresh, the pilot must re-authorize your application.

scopes.identity:basic: Your name and email address (always required)
scopes.identity:networks: Your online network IDs (VATSIM, IVAO, POSCON, APOC)
scopes.pilot:read: Read your pilot profile, rank, stats, and badges
scopes.pilot:write: Update your pilot preferences and holidays
scopes.flights:read: Read your bookings, PIREPs, claims, comments, and logbook
scopes.flights:write: Create bookings, file PIREPs, dispatch flights, and comment on PIREPs
scopes.activities:read: Read activity registrations, rosters, and community goals
scopes.activities:write: Register for activities and manage personal rosters

contribution_data.description: Extra data for contribution-based activities (community goals/challenges), null for regular activities

type.description: PIREP type, derived from the booking (e.g. scheduled, repositioning)

bonus_sum.description: Sum of all bonus points awarded

dispatch_id.description:
SimBrief flight plan identifier accepted by SimBrief's v2 API: the numeric
request_id from the OFP parameters, or the OFP's static_id. The ofp_id query
parameter appended by SimBrief's v1 dispatch redirect is NOT accepted.

network.description: Online network for the flight (Offline, VATSIM, IVAO, POSCON, APOC, PilotEdge, FSCloud, SayIntentions, Other)

pirep_id.description: Associated PIREP ID (null if no PIREP)

key.description: Group key (aircraft type name, network name, route type)

distance_flown.description: Total distance flown in nautical miles

needs_reply.description: Whether the pilot needs to reply to staff comments

examples: Brief turbulence caused high landing rate

pirep_id.description: ID of the associated PIREP, null while still processing

proof.description: Proof items — images resolved to full URLs, links preserved

counted.description: Whether this holiday counts against the allowance @example true

must_read.description: Whether the pilot must acknowledge this NOTAM before booking

url.description: Optional external URL for more information

is_read.description: Whether the authenticated pilot has read this NOTAM

start_showing.description: Timestamp from which the NOTAM should be displayed

stop_showing.description: Timestamp after which the NOTAM should no longer be displayed

name.description: Auto-generated name from the flight chain

hours_required.description: Whether hours is an enforced requirement @example true

points_required.description: Whether points is an enforced requirement @example false

bonus_required.description: Whether bonus is an enforced requirement @example false

hours_remaining.description: Hours still needed. Null if not a requirement. @example 120

points_remaining.description: Points still needed. Null if not a requirement. @example null

bonus_remaining.description: Bonus points still needed. Null if not a requirement. @example null

hub_id.description: Home hub ID, null if no hub assigned @example 3

prefer_honorary_rank.description: Whether the pilot prefers to display their honorary rank @example false

use_imperial_units.description: Whether the pilot uses imperial units @example false

holiday_allowance.description: Holiday allowance in days. Null if airline does not have a holiday feature

under_activity_grace.description: Whether pilot is under an activity grace period. Null if airline has no activity requirements

activity_whitelist.description: Whether pilot is on the activity whitelist. Null if airline has no activity requirements

activity_type.description: Activity type / category. Null if airline has no activity requirements

by_time_of_day.description: Breakdown by time of day (day vs night landings)

transport_year_to_date.description: Transport statistics for year to date

commenter_type.description: Whether the commenter is a pilot or staff member

commenter_name.description: Display name of the commenter, null when hidden

examples: The turbulence on approach caused the high landing rate — weather was unavoidable.

booking_id.description: Booking ID associated with this PIREP

aircraft_id.description: Aircraft ID used for this flight

block_time.description: Block time in minutes (off-blocks to on-blocks)

landing_rate.description: Landing rate in feet per minute

network.description: Online network used for the flight

need_reply.description: Whether the pilot needs to reply to staff comments

network.description: Online network for this position report

groundspeed.description: Groundspeed profile — seconds elapsed vs groundspeed in knots
